findings.rationale: Procedure P runs b7b9a971 and 9affd1f6 have the same source identity ac615159. Exactly 15 of 59 per-file coverage entries differ: pl_alo.c, pl_alo_qdplus.c (128/61 and 135/66), pl_alo_tables.c, pl_alo_ts.c, pl_alo_ts_level.c, pl_alo_ts_row0.c, pl_alo_ts_sum.c, pl_batch_row.c, pl_baw_admit.c, pl_baw_cert.c, pl_baw_map.c, pl_crr_lattice.c, pl_evaluate.c, pl_greeks.c, pl_solver.c. Each is on the engine path of the pooled batch tests. The program results are identical: every bit-exact vector test passes in all 11 builds of both runs, the tsan gate finds no data race and the msan gate no uninitialized read. Cause (concluded from the evidence and the flags, not proven with per-test profiles): the profile counter increments are not atomic, so concurrent increments of a hot counter can be lost. Both directions: (a) a lost increment can make a count 0, so llvm-cov reports a region that ran as uncovered (too low); (b) llvm-cov derives some counts as a parent counter minus a child counter, so a lost child increment can make a branch that never ran show as covered (too high). Until the framework fix, treat per-branch covered claims in these 15 files as unconfirmed; the Task 10c and 10d claims rely on files outside the 15 (pl_alo_points.c, pl_alo_edge.c) and on bit-exact vectors. Proposed fix (not done; a framework change): build the coverage variant with -fprofile-update=atomic, or export one profile per test (run the threaded tests under their own profile file) so per-test counts can be checked. Owner: framework (fw-release). No framework file is edited in this repository branch.
